subject.title: perf(sqlite): fast schema gates, background integrity verification, and downgrade protection

question: Should OpenClaw adopt this broad persisted-quarantine and fail-closed downgrade design now, including how updates to historic builds without schema metadata must behave?
rationale: The choice changes core startup and update failure semantics, adds durable state, and determines whether unknown historic target metadata is accepted, refused, or mapped; this is product and upgrade-policy intent rather than a mechanical repair.

options.title: Narrow and prove the protection first
options.body: Add a compatibility mapping or conservative refusal for known historic targets, retain the current integrity contract, and post real updater/gateway/doctor proof before considering the background verifier.

options.title: Approve the broad verifier design
options.body: Accept the new durable verification and quarantine model, but require documented legacy-target behavior plus upgrade and recovery proof before merge.

options.title: Split the verifier from downgrade protection
options.body: Land a narrowly proven schema-gate/update fix separately and continue the delayed verifier as a dedicated storage-policy proposal.

recommendation.title: Narrow and prove the protection first
recommendation.body: Add a compatibility mapping or conservative refusal for known historic targets, retain the current integrity contract, and post real updater/gateway/doctor proof before considering the background verifier.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent merged SQLite hardening ownership and the current proposal’s cross-cutting state/update scope make this the strongest available routing candidate.
